label: Tapered Transition
inheritsUnchanged: TP-C01, TP-C02, TP-C04 via super().validate(). TP-C03 is inherited but then OVERRIDDEN by the stricter TT-C05 -- see that constraint.

edges.note: THIS is Func3's real-design realisation, unlike GD-TP

mate-point asymmetry: GD-TT's weldL/weldR sit past a NIB offset from its own body; GD-TP's weldL/weldR sit directly at the body edge, no offset. Same join syntax on either side of a chain, different real distance depending on which one you're touching.
inner pipe of PiP bulkhead IS a GD-TT

designCode.summary: DNV — this component exists to satisfy DNV-ST-F101 Sec.5.6

scope.complianceStatus: DNV-compliant realisation of the GD-TP idea: taper (min slope 1:4) + NIB (Sec.5.6.1.7)
scope.whenGdTpStillRight: concept-stage screening, sweeps where taper isn't the variable, mesh-cost > fidelity-gain cases
scope.notPipelineSpecific: pipe is a constructor argument, not a fixed identity. Every equation here (dr, L_taper, NIB_dnv/NIB_min, OD_at) reads from self.pipe.OD_pipe/t_pipe, never a global or header-specific constant -- VERIFIED LIVE on a second BasePipeline built with GD-B's own OD_branch/t_branch (0.2731 m / 0.0159 m): default_for() re-derives correctly, L_NIB re-derives to 0.150 m (vs 0.200 m on STD_PIPELINE), extent (x_weld) becomes (-0.804, 0.804), and validate() passes. So a GD-TT sitting ON THE BRANCH LINE (inside a future GD-BrPipe chain, not yet an EDES node -- see edes:GD-B's own header pipe) is the same component, same equations, evaluated against the branch's own OD/t rather than the header's -- not a special case, not a different class. The `pipe` argument IS the mechanism that makes this true; no separate branch-variant of this file is needed.

free.name: n
free.meaning: TAPER SLOPE, expressed as 1:n -- one unit of radial rise per n units of axial run. Larger n means a LONGER, gentler taper. DNV's minimum is 4.
free.note: taper slope 1:n; default IS the DNV floor, fixed literal not pipe-relative

free.name: L_NIB
free.meaning: LENGTH OF THE UNDISTURBED LAND (the NIB) at each end, between the girth weld and the taper toe. Plain pipe at header OD, one at each end.
free.resolvedIn: __post_init__, not default_for() — inconsistent mechanism vs t_comp/L_comp

refused: L_taper — derived as n*dr, TypeError if passed

derived.name: NIB_min
derived.note: NIB_min IS the enforced floor (not raw NIB_dnv) — round-to-nearest falls below raw DNV value in 8/9 common line sizes, largest shortfall 22.5mm at 20in. Floor moved with the rounding so the module's own default cannot self-violate.

verifiedOnBranchPipe.note: same equation, GD-B's own default branch-pipe properties -- L_NIB re-derives to 0.150 m (vs 0.200 m on STD_PIPELINE), extent (x_weld) becomes (-0.804, 0.804). Confirms L_taper/L_NIB/extent are all pipe-relative throughout, not header-specific.

derived.name: dr
derived.note: same quantity as GD-TP.V, different name

derived.name: halfExtent
derived.expr: halfExtent = L_comp/2 + L_taper + L_NIB, where L_taper = n*dr, dr = (OD_comp - OD_pipe)/2, OD_comp = ID + 2*t_comp, and L_NIB defaults to NIB_min = round(4*l_e to nearest 50 mm) with l_e = sqrt(r_mean*t_pipe)/(3*(1-nu^2))^0.25 -- a property of the PIPE, not of this component
derived.meaning: HALF the component's axial footprint. extent = (centre_x - halfExtent, centre_x + halfExtent). Needed to place this component adjacent to another -- see edas:shared#/chaining.
derived.verifiedAt: the instance shown in verifiedWith below

geometry.meshAdvice: taper zones: min_elements=2, target=L_taper/2, grading ratio/run-up COMPUTED live from self.L_taper (fixed 30Aug26 — was hardcoded '~268:1'/'~0.88m', correct only at STD defaults, wrong by up to 175x elsewhere)

constraints.repair: increase n to at least 4 (1:4 minimum taper slope)
increase L_NIB to at least NIB_min, or omit L_NIB to use the computed default
raise t_comp above t_pipe, or use edes:GD-TP if a neutral section is wanted
constraints.note: edes:GD-TP relaxed TP-C03 to >= on 5Sep26 so a neutral section can carry a connector. That relaxation CANNOT extend here: taper length is n*dr with dr = (OD_comp - OD_pipe)/2, so an equal wall gives a ZERO-LENGTH taper. VERIFIED -- stations then coincide (taperL with bodyL, bodyR with taperR) producing two zero-length segments, the degenerate case guarded against everywhere else in this module. A tapered body with no taper is not a tapered body; it IS a edes:GD-TP, and the error message says so.

constraintEquivalence.method: probe vs live validate() incl. inherited chain

nonConstraints: no upper bound on n or t_comp/wall_ratio
no check that L_comp is short enough for a resolvable midspan moment (min_elements=1 in body zone permits 1 element at L_comp/D~2.46)

permittedConnections.verified: TaperedThickBody has no active_connectors of its own, so the inherited rows apply unchanged -- INCLUDING the 1Sep26 reversal of F from excluded to permitted, scoped to conMid, and the new W row scoped to the weld ends. This string previously read 'same Rz exclusion applies unchanged', which became stale the moment GD-TP's F row was reversed; corrected the same day. Inheritance means this file cannot drift from GD-TP on connection rows, but its own prose about them can, and did.

slots.note: canonical EDES name and component_spec node id agree here. So do edes:GD-TP's, since its rename on 4Sep26 (defect TP-D2, fixed) -- the corpus is now uniform on :weldL/:weldR

slots.position: mid-body, x = centre_x, between bodyL and bodyR
slots.note: IMPLEMENTED in component_spec 1Sep26 (was specification-only when first written the same day). VERIFIED LIVE: emitted at centre_x at MANDATORY priority, and both line sets subdivide at it so the connector attaches to an element boundary rather than an element interior. MANDATORY not because it is a section discontinuity -- it is not -- but because a connector node the mesher merged away would silently delete the connection it carries.

assemblyFeatures.status: the mate points an adjacent component ties to are weldL/weldR -- NOT taperL/taperR and NOT bodyL/bodyR. Those four are real, MANDATORY structural stations (section/slope discontinuities the mesher must not smear), but they sit INSIDE this component's own extent, not at its boundary. A chain join written as e.g. 'GD-TT.taperR = <neighbour>.weldL' would silently discard the outer NIB (L_NIB, the undisturbed run between the girth weld and the taper toe) and place the neighbouring component too close by exactly that length. extent = x_weld = (weldL, weldR) by construction (see Component.extent), so weldL/weldR are the only two stations that are simultaneously a real structural node AND the true edge of what this component owns.
assemblyFeatures.strictnessCaveat: whether these are OAMFeatures in NISTIR 7436's strict sense (a feature with at least one actual AssemblyFeatureAssociation) or merely Features depends on whether the component is mated in a given layout -- see edes:shared#/frameworks OAM.usedButLooser.AssemblyFeature candidacy. Unlike edes:GD-ST's optional connector slots, an inline component's weld ends are effectively always mated in any real chain; an unmated weld end is physically meaningful only at an ILS boundary.
assemblyFeatures.note: contrast edes:GD-TP, whose extent has no NIB at all -- its two mate points sit directly at the OD step, with no equivalent offset to get wrong.
assemblyFeatures.featureScopedTypes: candidateTypes differ BY FEATURE: weldL/weldR accept W only, conMid accepts F only. The component-level permittedConnections cannot express this -- see edes:shared#/oam/featureScopedConnections. Note also that taperL/taperR/bodyL/bodyR remain internal profile stations and are NOT features: nothing external mates at them.

behaviourDerived.mechanism: same as GD-TP but SPREAD by the taper; peak strain location reported at taper toe (catalogue ILS-TT), MOVES WITH L_NIB — ASSUMED provenance, not FEA-confirmed
behaviourDerived.mass: verified vs catalogue ILS-TT to 9 sig figs via numerical integration of the frustum taper (not closed-form)

usedInLayouts.note: Back-links to worked layouts containing this component, generated mechanically from the layout library on 1Sep26 -- not hand-written, so they cannot drift from it by authoring error, though they WILL go stale if the library changes and this is not regenerated. Their purpose is placement guidance: this file describes what the component IS and what its own constraints are, but says nothing about where along a header to put one or what to put either side of it. A worked archetype answers that by example. paramsUsed are the archetype's own values verbatim; anchors are published table rows that override them.

ILS-TT.purpose: The same wall build-up as ILS-TP, but eased in and out by a taper at each end, with a straight land before the girth weld.

defects.summary: mesh-grading note text was a hardcoded literal ('~268:1','~0.88m'), correct only at STD_PIPELINE defaults; wrong by up to 175x at the catalogue's own case

regressionCase.finding: taper does NOT fix representability — constant bore inherited unchanged, valve-as-GD-TT still returns OD_comp=0.4176 vs true 0.700
regressionCase.note: fixes CODE-COMPLIANCE half of Foundation Sec.3 failure#2, not the REPRESENTABILITY half

openQuestions: L_NIB __post_init__ resolution vs t_comp/L_comp default_for() — unify mechanism?
min_elements floor for short body zones?

assemblyFeatures now correctly NAMES weldL/weldR as this component's own mate points, but does not yet create the cross-component record that says what they mate TO (e.g. a future GD-HdPipe end, not yet an EDES node, or another component's weldL/lo directly). That is a separate, larger schema question -- whether mating becomes its own OAM AssemblyFeatureAssociation-shaped artifact type, where it would live, and how direction/derived-vs-given is encoded -- not resolved by this update.

inputsRequired.readAlso: edes:shared -- REQUIRED. ALSO edes:GD-TP: this component subclasses it, and t_comp, L_comp, t_comp_min and constraints TP-C01..C04 are inherited unchanged and documented THERE, not here. A reader with only this file does not see the two most important sizing parameters.

headerPipeline.why: as edes:GD-TP, plus the NIB length floor NIB_min = 4*sqrt(r*t)/(3(1-nu^2))^0.25 is computed from the header pipe's own radius and wall.

sizing.rule: EXACTLY ONE of t_comp or OD_comp is needed. They are not independent: constant bore means OD_comp = ID + 2*t_comp, where ID = OD_pipe - 2*t_pipe comes from the header. Supplying one determines the other.
sizing.t_comp: the EMITTABLE form. Pass it straight through to the definition.
sizing.OD_comp: ACCEPTED AS DESIGN INTENT, NOT EMITTABLE. The constructor refuses it (TypeError). Convert first: t_comp = (OD_comp - ID) / 2, then emit t_comp. This inversion is the single most likely place to get an instance wrong, because asking for a component by its outside diameter is the natural way to ask.
sizing.ifBothSupplied: check them against OD_comp = ID + 2*t_comp. If they disagree the person has over-specified: query rather than silently choosing one.
sizing.ifNeitherSupplied: t_comp defaults to 2.5*t_pipe. Emitting nothing keeps that default LIVE and pipe-relative -- see the omission rule. Emitting the computed number pins it. These are different design states.
sizing.note: Inherited from edes:GD-TP -- same rule, same inversion, same TP-C03 floor.

placement.centre_x: REQUIRED. See usedInLayouts (ILS-TT) for a worked precedent, or query.

optional.n: taper slope 1:n, defaults to 4.0 (the DNV minimum). Raising it lengthens the taper.
optional.L_NIB: undisturbed land each side, defaults to NIB_min. Do not go below it -- constraint.

inputsRequired.ifMissing: Anything listed as required, having no default, and not supplied by the person must be QUERIED. Do not assume a value and do not carry one over from a worked example -- a precedent shows what was once chosen, not what this case needs.
